editorial:
Imagine taking a trip to Amsterdam with your kid only to find out they don't actually want to come home with you. That is exactly what happens to Hannah when she brings her non-binary teen, Frances, to visit their grandfather, Jimpa. The movie feels like a warm hug mixed with a bit of a family fight. You get to see this sweet bond grow between a teenager and their gay grandfather, while Hannah struggles to keep things under control. It is a grounded story about how different generations see the world and the friction that happens when a parent realizes their child is growing up into someone they don't fully understand yet.

The acting is the best part here because the conversations feel real and not scripted. You will love how Jimpa brings out a side of Frances that Hannah never sees. The pacing is a bit slow at times, but it helps you feel the weight of the family history. If you are looking for a heartfelt story about acceptance, you should definitely check this out. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for a crisp look at the city, or just rent it on Apple TV for a cozy movie night at home.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Hannah finally stops fighting and agrees to let Frances stay in Amsterdam for a while. She realizes that Jimpa provides a kind of support and understanding that she cannot give right now. The movie ends with a touching goodbye where Hannah and Frances make peace. It wraps up with the idea that love means letting go and trusting your child to find their own path in life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family stories about growth and acceptance.
